title: Adaptive span allocator and hybrid prefetch policy for paged-attention KV cache
creator: Kunal Shah
description:
Problem: For long-sequence workloads using paged attention, current KV allocation is chunk-oriented and tends to produce small high-fragmentation allocations when prefill patterns vary across tenants and models. This leads to: higher GPU memory overhead, suboptimal kernel placement (kernels cannot colocate hot KV spans), and prefill stalls during decode when prefetch streams compete for limited allocation windows.

Goal: Implement an adaptive span allocator that groups logical KV allocations into variable-length spans based on access hotness and kernel affinity, and a hybrid prefetch policy that mixes conservative hysteresis-driven prefetching with opportunistic aggressive prefetch for predicted hot spans. Outcome targets: reduce fragmentation by >35%, reduce prefill-induced decode stalls p95 by 30%, and reduce per-token memory cost for multi-tenant serving by at least 20% in our benchmark suite.
acceptance_criteria: Span allocator implemented in runtime with per-shard span metadata and API to query span hotness and kernel affinity
Hybrid prefetch policy integrated with request scheduler and KV manager (config flags: prefetch.mode=hybrid, prefetch.hysteresis_ms)
Benchmarks: fragmentation metric (free segments count / allocated segments) reduced by >= 35% on long-seq Llama-like workloads compared to baseline
Decode throughput regression: p50 token latency unchanged (within 5%) and p95 improved by >= 20% under mixed-tenant load
Graceful fallback: disable span allocation and revert to legacy page allocator via runtime flag with no request drops
Design doc and implementation PR merged, smoke tests and end-to-end perf dashboards updated
notes: Key idea: allocate variable-length spans (span = contiguous set of KV pages) and maintain an epoch-decay hotness score per span. Hot spans are candidates for aggressive prefetch and kernel colocation.
Span sizing heuristic: base on recent stream length distribution + model kernel (e.g., flash-attn vs. tiled-attn) to prefer sizes aligned to kernel prefetch granularity to reduce partial-page waste.

Hybrid prefetch: two modes within single policy: (1) hysteresis conservative prefetching for cold spans (wait until access frequency crosses threshold for X ms), (2) predictive aggressive prefetch triggered when sequence pattern and tokenizer heuristics indicate continuing hot run.

Kernel-aware placement: annotate spans with preferred kernel class so scheduler can try to place decoder/encoder kernels that use same memory locality as the spans; helps reduce cross-kernel page thrash.
Soft-compact: background compaction merges adjacent low-hotness spans during low-load windows to reduce fragmentation without blocking prefill paths.
Telemetry: add metrics span_hotness_bucket, span_count_by_size, span_prefetch_hits, span_eviction_reasons to runtime telemetry surface for Console dashboards.
decisions: Use epoch-based decay (half-life 15 minutes) rather than LRU per-page because we need temporal smoothing across bursts and resumptions
Represent spans as first-class metadata instead of explicit reshaping of existing allocator; this minimizes intrusive changes to memory allocator internals
Prefer conservative default policy (prefetch.mode=hybrid with hysteresis defaults) and expose aggressive knobs behind feature flag for dedicated capacity customers
Compaction will run opportunistically and not during high decode tail to avoid SLO regressions

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive prefetch may increase peak GPU memory and cause OOMs during multi-tenant spikes. Mitigation: enforce per-tenant soft-reserve and prefetch backpressure when memory_util > configured threshold.
Risk: Background compaction may contend with decode for GPU bandwidth. Mitigation: compaction only runs when GPU util < 40% and rate-limited by tokens/sec budget.
Risk: Incorrect kernel affinity predictions reduce benefit. Mitigation: fall back to span-level LRU and collect kernel-affinity telemetry to iterate predictor model.
experiments_and_metrics: Experiment A (long-seq Llama-like, 12 tenants): fragmentation reduced 37% vs baseline; GPU memory per-tenant decreased 19%; p95 decode latency improved 24%
Experiment B (mixed short+long sequences): p50 stable, p95 improved 14% when scheduler colocation enabled, otherwise only 6%
Memory safety: aggressive prefetch with current predictor exceeded memory watermark in 2/50 stress runs; hysteresis reduced incidence to 0/50
